IRAN REFUSES TO REOPEN STRAIT OF HORMUZ Ending the Iran war is reportedly the main focus of Rezaei-Putin talks, according to Al Mayadeen. Iran insists the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until its seven conditions are met, ruling out negotiations over that decision.

Qatar-led mediation has gained momentum, with talks held in Tehran and Doha, while Vice President JD Vance is reportedly pushing for a negotiated settlement. DEMOCRATS SWEEP CONGRESS. FED HIKE BETS RETREAT. Following the midterm results, December Fed hike odds have fallen from above 80% to 67%. Prediction markets now put the chance of a hold at 33%, its highest since mid-September.

The model reportedly identified 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and helped identify and develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including 588 previously unknown issues. ANTHROPIC IPO ODDS PLUNGE AS TECH SELLOFF DEEPENS Anthropic's chances of going public in 2026 have fallen below 60% on Kalshi, down from nearly 90% before the midterms. Investors are reportedly targeting a $1.5T–$1.6T valuation for the Claude developer, down from earlier estimates near $2T. Despite the tech selloff, prediction-market traders still expect an IPO within months. Sources: Kalshi, The Wall Street Journal

US WARNS OF ONGOING CYBER THREAT TO INDUSTRIAL REFRIGERATION US officials issued a cybersecurity warning Thursday, citing an ongoing threat to industrial refrigeration systems. Authorities urged every organization relying on refrigeration to assume it could be targeted.

Hundreds of emails reveal coordination to return over 100 Iranians on three flights in September and December 2025 and January 2026. Plans for further deportations continued into October. SOUTH KOREA’S KOSPI PLUNGES OVER 8%, TRIGGERING CIRCUIT BREAKER South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI index ($KS11) crashed more than 8% in early Friday trading, triggering a 20-minute market-wide trading halt. The sharp decline comes amid a broader global selloff in technology stocks.

Semiconductors crashed 12%, with Nvidia down 9% and AMD down 17%. AI infrastructure stocks suffered heavily: CoreWeave -10%, Nebius -15%, as CoreWeave’s credit default spreads hit record highs. JAPAN’S PRIME MINISTER WARNS OF GLOBAL MARKET VOLATILITY Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says Japan is closely monitoring global markets following the US midterm elections. Takaichi acknowledged sharp declines in AI and semiconductor stocks, warning that volatility is affecting economies worldwide. She pledged to strengthen Japan’s economy by supporting industries where the country holds competitive advantages.

TEXAS GOVERNOR-ELECT CALLS FOR HALT TO NEW DATA CENTERS Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants data-center development paused until new laws protect residents. “We need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have those protections,” she told CNN. Hinojosa also said Elon Musk’s companies can operate in Texas, but on her administration’s terms, despite Musk backing her Republican opponent.

US CHIP STOCKS SURGE AS AI SECTOR REBOUNDS FROM BRUTAL SELLOFF Semiconductor stocks rallied sharply in Friday's premarket, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF up nearly 5% and Nasdaq 100 futures gaining 1.3%. Lam Research +9%, Micron +7.5%, Marvell +7%, AMD and Applied Materials +6%, while CoreWeave rebounded 6.3%. The recovery follows Thursday's AI rout and heavy Asian losses, with South Korea's KOSPI closing down over 6%.

S&P 500 FUTURES FACE FURTHER DOWNSIDE AS BEARISH SIGNALS INTENSIFY S&P 500 E-mini futures broke below key support at 7,386, confirming an acceleration of the bearish trend that began October 6. Downside targets: 7,317, 7,240 and 7,176. Initial resistance: 7,675. The daily market condition is oversold, but any rebound is considered corrective. EURO STOXX 50 futures also face downside risk below 6,032, while a break above 6,251 could signal a recovery toward 6,399.

PROTESTERS STORM MICROSOFT DATA CENTER IN THE NETHERLANDS Around 100 protesters entered Microsoft's data center near Amsterdam on Friday, opposing the expansion of AI infrastructure. Activists from Geef Tegengas accused AI data centers of consuming local resources and harming the environment.

SOFTBANK PLUNGES 59% AS DEBT-FUELED AI BETS UNRAVEL SoftBank shares fell another 10.8% Friday, extending losses to 59% since early June. The company added $40.4 billion in debt over 12 months to fund AI investments, including $64 billion in OpenAI. Meanwhile, Arm shares have plunged 51% since June 30, weakening SoftBank's asset backing as credit-default swaps rise and bond prices fall. IRAN SIGNALS PROGRESS IN US NEGOTIATIONS Iranian sources say Tehran is responding positively to the latest proposal submitted by mediators, according to Al Arabiya. Iran remains open to negotiations but insists that Washington take concrete steps to build trust, with reciprocal confidence-building measures and respect for Tehran's demands. Sources also say Ghalibaf faces no restrictions in managing the talks.

FED'S DALY WELCOMES STRONG JOBS REPORT BUT WARNS ON INFLATION Fed's Mary Daly calls October's jobs report “good news”, expressing optimism about the US workforce. However, she stresses that wage growth isn't booming and real wages are falling. On inflation, Daly says prices have been rising too quickly for too long and she wants greater confidence in the inflation outlook.

The proposal would invoke Section 501(p) of the tax code, potentially bypassing lengthy IRS review procedures. TRUMP ANNOUNCES STEPHEN MILLER AS CHIEF OF STAFF FROM MONDAY

TRUMP NAMES STEPHEN MILLER AS NEW WHITE HOUSE CHIEF OF STAFF President Trump announces that Stephen Miller will become White House Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9. Miller, currently Deputy Chief of Staff and one of Trump's most trusted advisers, will replace Susie Wiles, who is moving to Trump's political operation. Trump praised Wiles for doing an outstanding job.
